 Sign in All Blacks name side for Wales clash in Cardiff
 All Blacks 2 days ago By:   Alan Brown All Blacks Head Coach Dave Rennie has named his team to play Wales at Principality Stadium in Cardiff in Round Five of the Nations Championship. Fullback Beauden Barrett will captain the All Blacks in a Test for the first time, in his 149 th  Test. Loose forward Anton Segner and wing Fehi Fineanganofo will both make their first Test starts, Segner in his fifth Test and Fineanganofo in his second. 
 Kick off 2.10PM local time (3.10AM Sunday 15 November NZT), LIVE on Sky Sport. Highlights available on allblacks.com and the All Blacks and Black Ferns app. Follow the official live blog HERE .

 WATCH: Go inside All Blacks camp in the latest episode of Behind the Fern
 S2, E13: Behind the Fern: The Quiet Hero Behind the All Blacks 10 Changes to the team that faced Scotland
 The team includes ten changes to the match-day 23 that played Scotland in round four of the Nations Championship last weekend, eight of them in the starting side. Prop George Bower, hooker Asafo Aumua, Segner and halfback Cortez Ratima move from the reserves into the starting side, while lock Josh Lord, first five-eighth Richie Mo’unga, midfielder Anton Lienert-Brown and Fineanganofo come into the team. Hooker George Bell, prop Xavier Numia, lock Jamie Hannah, loose forwards Ethan Blackadder and Leicester Fainga’anuku, and halfback Kyle Preston join prop Pasilio Tosi and outside back Rieko Ioane in the reserves.
 WATCH: Dave Rennie talks through the 23 to face Wales in Cardiff
 Who’s In? All Blacks Reveal Changes for Wales Test | Press Conference (Cardiff) Huge honour for Beauden Barrett in his 149th Test
 “Beauden brings such valuable experience and is massively respected by us all. Captaining the All Blacks in a Test is an honour that I know he doesn’t take lightly, so it’ll be a proud day for him and his whānau,” Rennie said. “We have created good depth in this group and there is a lot of competition for places. We have selected a strong side with 783 caps."
 “ ” Wales are a proud rugby nation and building nicely under Steve Tandy. We are well aware of the threat they pose and the challenge of playing in front of a passionate crowd at Principality Stadium. Dave Rennie WATCH: All Blacks playmaker Damian McKenzie on his evolution in the black jersey
 Inside The Black Jersey: Ep 7 | Damian McKenzie and the road to the Nations Championship final MATCH FACTS 
 This will be the 39 th  Test between the All Blacks and Wales, who first met in 1905.
 Asafo Aumua and Quinn Tupaea will face Wales for the first time in their All Blacks careers.
 Beauden Barrett will play his 149 th  Test, to pass Richie McCaw in the all-time records and be second only to Sam Whitelock on 153 Tests. 
 Beauden Barrett now has 50 All Blacks Test tries, one ahead of Doug Howlett, and closing in on Will Jordan’s record of 56.
 Anton Lienert-Brown will play his 99 th  match for the All Blacks.
